content.text: # Review Task — missing test coverage only You are reviewing a code change **you did not write**. You have one narrow job. **Your only subject: behaviour that has no test at all.** Not weak tests — another reviewer covers those. Not the implementation's quality. Not style. **Absent** tests. If you find something outside your remit, drop it. ## Why this needs saying It is far easier to look at a test that exists and judge it than to notice a test that is not there. Nothing draws your attention to an absence. You will not find these by reading the test file, because everything in it looks fine — the gaps are precisely what is not in it. So do not read the test file first. **Build the list of what should be tested before you look at what is tested.** Then compare. ## The procedure Follow it in this order. The order is the whole method. **Step 1 — Build the required list, from the specification only.** Read the task specification. Write down every distinct behaviour it requires. Include: - every case it names explicitly, including edge cases and error conditions; - every acceptance criterion; - every entry point it asks for — a command line, a public function, an exported symbol; - every stated constraint, since "must never X" is a testable claim. Number them. Do not open the test file yet. **Step 2 — Build the surface list, from the diff only.** List every callable the change adds or modifies: functions, methods, `main()`, argument parsing, each branch of a conditional that changes behaviour. Note which are entry points — anything a user or another program calls directly. **Step 3 — Now read the tests.** For each item in lists 1 and 2, find the test that covers it. Record the test's name, or record `NONE`. **Step 4 — Verify each `NONE` before reporting it.** Do not trust your reading. For each gap: - `grep` the test file for the function, flag, or behaviour name; - if you still believe it is untested, **break it** — change that behaviour in the source so it is obviously wrong, run the full suite, and confirm the suite still passes. Then restore. A gap you have proven with a passing suite is a finding. A gap you merely did not spot a test for is not. ## What to look for especially These are the gaps that recur, in rough order of how often they are missed: - **The command-line entry point.** Argument parsing, exit codes, what reaches stderr, `--help`. Logic tested through a pure function while `main()` is never invoked is the single most common gap. - **Error paths.** The spec says bad input must produce a clean message; no test feeds it bad input. - **The empty and zero cases.** No items, an empty file, a count of nothing. - **Constraints stated as prohibitions.** "Must never write to X", "must not modify Y" — testable, rarely tested. - **Output written to a file** as opposed to returned as a value. - **A branch that only runs on unusual input** — the `else` nobody exercises. ## Report Output only these blocks, nothing before or after. ``` ### FINDING axis: missing-coverage file: severity: high | medium | low confidence: verified | suspected requirement: gap: proof: ``` `severity: high` means the specification explicitly requires the behaviour and nothing tests it. `confidence: verified` requires a `proof` — a break you actually made, with the suite passing anyway. Without one it is `suspected`, and you may report at most two suspected findings. **Restore every file you touched.** Confirm with `git status` and say so. End with exactly one line: ``` SUMMARY: missing-coverage= blocking= requirements-listed= requirements-uncovered= restored= ``` `requirements-listed` is how many items your step 1 list contained. **If that number is 0 you did not do the job** — the method starts with building the list, and an all-clear that skipped step 1 is worthless. --- ## The change under review Branch `worker/f03-status-page`, based on `main`. The repository is checked out at the branch tip, so every file is readable and the test suite is runnable. Get the diff with either: - `git diff main...HEAD` — run it yourself, or - read the file `C:\Dev\homelab\experiments\local-llm-worker\evaluation\runs\rv3-missing-coverage\under-review.patch`, which holds the same diff. ## Tool rules - **Never start a process that does not exit on its own** -- a server, a watcher, anything with `serve`, `--watch`, or a `while True:` loop. The bash tool waits for the whole process group, so `&` does not detach it and the call hangs until the run is killed. Exercise such code only through its test suite, or through a Python snippet that starts it in a thread and shuts it down in the same snippet. If you are about to type a command that would still be running a minute later, do not run it. - Run the test suite and short one-off commands freely; nothing else. --- ## The task specification the change was meant to satisfy # Task: a status page showing what the local worker is doing right now **Create `scripts/status_page.py`.** Then **create `tests/test_status_page.py`**. Change no other file. ## Current behavior Every pipeline run — a task, a review, a triage — gets a directory under `evaluation/runs//`. Since today each runner writes `started.json` there the moment the directory exists: ```json { "kind": "task", // or "review", "triage" "task_id": "f02-fix-03-readonly-test", "title": "pin the read-only constraint with a test", "started_at": "2026-08-19T04:31:47+00:00", "branch": "worker/f02-fix-03" // plus other kind-specific keys; ignore them } ``` When the run ends, one terminal file appears beside it — `run.json` for a task, `review.json` for a review, `triage.json` for a triage — and each carries a top-level `recorded_at` in the same ISO-8601 form (search each runner for `"recorded_at"`). Older run directories predate the marker and have no `started.json`. **Nothing reads any of this while a run is in flight.** To know what the worker is doing you open a terminal and look at the log. The person who wants to glance at it from another room cannot. ## Desired behavior One script, standard library only, no new dependencies: ``` python scripts/status_page.py status [--runs DIR] [--now ISO8601] python scripts/status_page.py serve [--runs DIR] [--host HOST] [--port N] ``` - `status` prints one JSON object to stdout and exits 0: ```json { "generated_at": "...", "current": { "task_id": "...", "kind": "task", "title": "...", "started_at": "...", "duration_seconds": 123.0 } | null, "running": [ ...every in-flight run, same shape, newest started first... ], "recent": [ ...finished runs, newest first, same shape plus "finished_at"... ], "unreadable": [ "", ... ], "ignored": } ``` `current` is the newest entry of `running`, or `null` when nothing is in flight. `recent` is capped at 10. `--now` pins the clock for tests; without it, use the real UTC time. - `serve` runs an HTTP server — `http.server` from the standard library — that answers `GET /` with a plain HTML page and `GET /status.json` with exactly the object above, computed fresh on every request. Anything else is a 404. The page shows: the current run's title, kind, id and elapsed time as `m:ss` (or "idle" when `current` is null), and a short table of recent runs. It refreshes itself with ``. No JavaScript, no external assets, inline CSS only. Everything written into the page passes through `html.escape`. - `--host` defaults to `127.0.0.1`, `--port` to `8765`. Not `0.0.0.0` — this workstation's local endpoints are loopback-only on purpose, and the page has no authentication. Duration rules — the only arithmetic in the task, so get it exactly right: - a run is **running** when `started.json` exists and none of `run.json`, `review.json`, `triage.json` does; `duration_seconds = now − started_at`; - a run is **finished** when a terminal file exists; `duration_seconds = recorded_at − started_at` and `finished_at = recorded_at`; - parse every timestamp with `datetime.fromisoformat`; they carry offsets, so subtraction is timezone-correct without any string handling; - a directory whose `started.json` or terminal file is missing, truncated or not an object goes in `unreadable` by name, never raises, never stops the listing; - a directory with no `started.json` at all is counted in `ignored` and otherwise skipped. ## Key interfaces - `scripts/run_task.py` — `write_started()` (line ~76) is the writer of `started.json`; its `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds")` is the timestamp format on both ends. - `evaluation/runs/` — the real data. `f02-fix-03-readonly-test/` is a finished task, `rv2-errors/` a finished review, `tr-f02-claude/` a finished triage; all three predate `started.json`, so against the real directory they are `ignored` today. Do not add files to any real run directory. - `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` with a `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` subclass; bind port `0` in tests and read `server.server_address[1]`. ## Seams under test - **The pure function** — something like `collect_status(runs_dir: Path, now: datetime) -> dict` — over a fixture `runs/` tree built by hand in a temporary directory. **[REQUIRED]** - **`main()` through the command line** — `status` as a subprocess against the fixture, asserting exit code 0 and that stdout parses as JSON. Build a small `run_cli` helper with `subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(SCRIPT), ...], capture_output=True, text=True)`. **[REQUIRED]** - **The HTTP server** — start it on port 0 in a thread, `urllib.request.urlopen` both paths and a bogus one, shut it down in `tearDown`. **[REQUIRED]** This is the seam that catches a handler that works in the author's head and 500s in a browser. ## Cases the tests must cover | Case | Source of truth for the assertion | | --- | --- | | Running: `started_at: "2026-08-19T10:00:00+00:00"`, `--now 2026-08-19T10:05:30+00:00`, no terminal file | `duration_seconds == 330.0`, state running, it is `current` | | Running across offsets: `started_at: "2026-08-19T12:00:00+02:00"`, now `"2026-08-19T10:00:05+00:00"` | **`5.0`** — verified by `datetime.fromisoformat` subtraction; string arithmetic gets this wrong by two hours | | Finished task: `started_at: "2026-08-19T10:00:00+00:00"`, `run.json` with `recorded_at: "2026-08-19T10:06:32+00:00"` | `duration_seconds == 392.0`, `finished_at == "2026-08-19T10:06:32+00:00"`, appears in `recent`, not in `running` | | Finished review with only `review.json`; finished triage with only `triage.json` | each is recognised as finished by its own terminal file name | | Two running runs started `10:00:00` and `10:03:00` | `current` is the `10:03:00` one; `running` lists both, newest first | | Nothing running, two finished | `current is None`, `recent` newest-first by `started_at` | | Twelve finished runs | `len(recent) == 10`, the ten newest | | `started.json` containing `{"kind": "task", "title": ` (truncated) | that directory name is in `unreadable`; every other run is still listed; exit code 0 | | `started.json` containing `[1, 2, 3]` | same — in `unreadable`, no traceback | | A directory with `run.json` but no `started.json`; a stray file `runs/notes.txt` | `ignored == 1`, the file is not counted or listed, nothing raises | | `--runs` pointing at a directory that does not exist | `current is None`, `running == []`, `recent == []`, exit 0, **and the directory is not created** — assert on the filesystem | | HTTP `GET /status.json` over a tree with only finished runs | status 200, `Content-Type` starts with `application/json`, body parses to the same object the pure function returns for that tree once `generated_at` is removed from both — finished durations do not depend on the clock, so only that key differs | | HTTP `GET /` | status 200, `Content-Type` starts with `text/html`, body contains the current run's title | | HTTP `GET /` with a current title of `x` | body contains `<b>x</b>` and not `x` | | HTTP `GET /nope` | status 404 | | `serve` and `status` never write | snapshot the set of paths under the fixture before and after a `collect_status` call and two HTTP requests; the sets are equal | ## Out of scope - Do not modify `scripts/run_task.py`, `run_review.py`, `run_triage.py` or any existing file. - Do not add files under `evaluation/runs/`. Tests use a temporary directory only. - No third-party packages, no JavaScript, no external fonts or stylesheets. - No authentication, no write endpoints, no configuration file. Flags only. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `python scripts/status_page.py status` against the real `evaluation/runs/` exits 0 and prints valid JSON (today that means `current: null` and a non-zero `ignored`). - [ ] Every case in the table behaves as its source of truth requires. - [ ] The read-only test fails if `runs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` is inserted at the top of `collect_status`. Verify this yourself: insert it, watch the test fail, remove it, and quote the failure in your summary. - [ ] `python -m ruff check scripts tests && python -m pytest -q` passes. Baseline on `main` is **71 passed, 6 subtests passed**, ruff clean, so any other failure is a regression introduced here. - [ ] Return a concise summary of what you built, the design choices you made and why, and anything left unresolved. ## Deliberately left to you - whether `recent` is sorted by `started_at` or `finished_at` — say which in the summary; - how `m:ss` renders hours (`1:02:03` or `62:03`) — pick one, test it; - whether the page shows the `branch` key when present; - the handler's logging — `http.server` prints every request to stderr by default; silence it or keep it, but say which. ## Notes - Conventions in this repo: `from __future__ import annotations`, `SCREAMING_CASE` constants, functions returning plain `dict`, private helpers prefixed `_`, `pathlib` only. Tests: `unittest.TestCase`, `sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))` then a flat `from status_page import (...) # noqa: E402`, fixtures in `setUp` with `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()`, torn down in `tearDown`, file ends `if __name__ == "__main__": unittest.main()`. Read `tests/test_run_task.py` for the shape. - `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` for the default clock; keep a `now` parameter on the pure function so the tests never depend on the wall clock. - `ThreadingHTTPServer.shutdown()` must be called from a different thread than `serve_forever()`; start the server with `threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)`. - Ruff runs with defaults, so an unused import in either file fails the acceptance command.
